scope: Corollary 4.10 (Primal surrounding circuits) of the manuscript “Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps” (preprints/Canonical-conformal-limits-of-subcritical-FK-planar-maps-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e7dab39caf778176), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let B0 ⋐ B1 ⋐ B2 ⋐ B3 be concentric closed disks in a planar reference chart. Suppose a closed primal walk has projection in int(B2) \ B1 and nonzero winding about B0. For all sufficiently accurate correspondences it contains a simple primal circuit Cn with the following properties. The closed side Ωn of Cn opposite the exterior of B3 contains every lift whose projection lies in B0, is disjoint from every lift projecting outside B3, and satisfies Pn(Ωn) ⊂ B3. The circuit uses a subset of the walk’s edges with multiplicities discarded; for nonnegative edge costs its cost is at most the cost of that walk. The conclusion holds in a protected bilateral window as well.
